semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode' is read by the candidate as requiring an unconditional default initial edge, and the exact source/model facts (transition:line:20 with trigger Power_On, diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, and verify_facts refutation of the initial-entry check) establish that the sole root-scope initial edge is conditional rather than unconditional. This is a precise, exactly-bound semantic fact even though predicate_id is null (S2 could not be closed via strict primary rebinding), so grounding is established per the D boundary rule that a predicate-null route does not erase a precise issue. A second competent reading remains available: since the NL itself names the power-on event, a triggered pseudostate edge keyed to that same event is a plausible alternate interpretation of 'unconditional' default entry, which is why this survives as an undercutting defeater rather than being defeated outright.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The NL phrase 'when power on' could itself be read as licensing a triggered initial edge rather than requiring an unconditional default entry, so the existing conditional edge on Power_On might be viewed as a competent, if unconventional, realization of the power-on-triggered entry, leaving only the downstream reachability consequence as the residual defect.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL3 requires an unconditional root-scope initial pseudostate edge into HumanDrivingMode on power-on; the closed model's only root-scope initial edge (transition:line:20, [*]->HumanDriving) carries trigger Power_On and is diagnosed INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, and verify_facts explicitly refutes the initial-entry check (has_trigger=true).

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability of the power-on initial edge, event-consumer coverage for Power_On, termination stability for Power_Off->FinalState, and the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition group. This directly affects NL3-INIT-1 (initial_entry) as a wrong/conditional owner-local edge, and licenses a derived event_consumer_coverage obligation because Power_On's sole consumer transition is structurally unreachable from init. The AutonomousMode internal Navigating/Parking exits to [*] both carry effect R45RouteToken=6 and no guard, while the outer Autonomous->HumanDriving transition (line 19) requires guard R45RouteToken==6 -- this composite completion pattern is a UML sub-machine final/exit-to-guard macro, which is a legitimate closed pattern, not itself a defect, so NL4.2 endpoint/guard/event contracts are examined against this exact routing token mechanism. NL5 termination (Power_Off -> HumanDriving -> [*]) is a genuine final pseudostate exit from HumanDriving with no re-entry possible, so termination is satisfied on its face notwithstanding the root initial-entry defect (kept as a separate obligation). Root reachability (all 5 states) is proved by verify_facts, so no additional reachability contract is warranted beyond the initial-entry issue itself.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode' is read by the candidate as requiring an unconditional default initial edge, and the exact source/model facts (transition:line:20 with trigger Power_On, diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, and verify_facts refutation of the initial-entry check) establish that the sole root-scope initial edge is conditional rather than unconditional. This is a precise, exactly-bound semantic fact even though predicate_id is null (S2 could not be closed via strict primary rebinding), so grounding is established per the D boundary rule that a predicate-null route does not erase a precise issue. A second competent reading remains available: since the NL itself names the power-on event, a triggered pseudostate edge keyed to that same event is a plausible alternate interpretation of 'unconditional' default entry, which is why this survives as an undercutting defeater rather than being defeated outright.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The NL phrase 'when power on' could itself be read as licensing a triggered initial edge rather than requiring an unconditional default entry, so the existing conditional edge on Power_On might be viewed as a competent, if unconventional, realization of the power-on-triggered entry, leaving only the downstream reachability consequence as the residual defect.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL3 requires an unconditional root-scope initial pseudostate edge into HumanDrivingMode on power-on; the closed model's only root-scope initial edge (transition:line:20, [*]->HumanDriving) carries trigger Power_On and is diagnosed INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, and verify_facts explicitly refutes the initial-entry check (has_trigger=true).

semantic_adjudication.basis: candidate, event_consumers fact, and diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE of dossier 0030:r1:i4 bound to transition:line:20, state:HumanDriving:line:9; defeater_evidence_reference_catalog for this obligation
semantic_adjudication.reason: The derived operational-coverage obligation requires the Power_On event to have a reachable consumer transition from a genuine top-level initial entry; the exact deterministic fact inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers explicitly lists reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for Power_On despite a declared consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:20], corroborated by diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE and verify_facts refutation of event-consumer:Power_On. Per the property-preserving adjudication protocol, a declared consumer does not rebut a contract requiring a reachable consumer, so this is established despite the null predicate_id (a W boundary only). The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal that HumanDriving might be reachable by some other means is a weaker/different property (state reachability, not event-consumer-transition reachability) and does not exactly rebut this coverage fact, but since it is not conclusively excluded by an exact supplied fact in this dossier, it survives as an undercutting defeater on the narrow question of practical consequence, without disturbing the core established violation.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: Because HumanDriving may be reachable_from_initial via some other mechanism the dossier does not fully spell out, one could argue the practical effect of Power_On firing is moot since HumanDriving is entered regardless; however this weaker reachability-of-target property does not rebut the exact reachable-consumer-transition property that the deterministic event-consumer analysis specifically refutes.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The Power_On event must have a reachable consumer transition from the root's genuine initial entry so the required HumanDrivingMode entry can actually fire; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers shows consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:20] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[], and diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE plus verify_facts refutation confirm this.
